story.what_it_does: Aptus lends for homes and small businesses to self-employed, low and middle income customers, mainly in small towns and rural South India. It had 397 branches as of September 2026, with loan book (AUM) of ₹14,177 crore.
story.plans: Management guided to 22-24% AUM growth in FY27 and later said around 22%. It plans 25 more branches in Q2 FY27 and expects asset quality to normalise by the end of FY27.
story.moat: The notes give no explicit competitive advantage. Strong profitability (ROA about 7.7-7.9%, ROE about 20%) and a very high capital ratio (69.2% in Sep 2026) suggest a strong position in its niche, but the notes do not say why.

scenarios.story: Growth stays around 20-22% as new branches add loans, and delinquencies normalise by the end of FY27 as management expects. Profit keeps growing with high returns and a strong capital cushion.
signals_to_watch: Gross NPA falling back from 1.68% toward earlier levels near 1.2-1.5%
AUM growth moving toward the 22% FY27 guidance

scenarios.story: AUM keeps growing near 20-21% and profit grows in the high teens, with returns staying around 7.7% ROA and 20% ROE. Asset quality stays a little weaker than a year ago, with seasonal swings.
Delinquencies keep rising, especially from the NBFC business, so credit costs eat into profit. Growth stays near 20%, short of the 22-24% guidance, and the promised normalisation slips.
signals_to_watch: AUM growth falling below 20% against the FY27 guidance
